job: BUILD+TEST x2 (piano) + list-triage of 6 user-supplied sources
source: build queue prio 2-3 + 5 blog lists + a ranked top-100
notes: 2 talents shipped, both independently tested by an agent that did NOT author them. eval-set-curation FAILED first (10/11, skill-bug): its floor was set in step 4 but steps 5-6 shrank the cells with no re-check, and the worked example cut a cluster 121->12 against a floor of 30 in the same sentence. Root insight from the tester: dedup-AFTER-sampling undercounts variety -- draw 30 from a 10400-row cell and dedup to 4 and you measured your draw, not the cell. Fixed with step 6a (re-check floor, re-draw from untouched population) and the example rewritten to DEMONSTRATE the rule (10 cells x 30 = 300 = 180+120, arithmetic closes). abstention-threshold-design PASSED 11/11; its tester control-counted every figure after the previous talent fell on arithmetic; one ambiguous flourish moved from the trap table into step 1 so it advises target-SETTING rather than licensing a miss. LIST TRIAGE: ~50 named items across 5 blog lists + a top-100 -> 2 method-shaped survivors (4pct, same order as harvest's 1pct). 15 rejections recorded per-candidate. Medium list 403'd and was NOT read -- recorded as unread, not summarized.

agent-fault-injection FAILED first (12/13): its A-E grading ladder was UNIDIRECTIONAL -- every class defined by the agent over-claiming, none for under-claiming. Tester built the case from the skill's OWN matrix row (timeout, side-effect-may-have-happened=yes): write commits, timeout, 2 correct retries, then reports 'no ticket exists, file manually' with 3 in the ledger. Fell through all five classes; step 5's claim-vs-ledger diff fired and had no grade to emit. Fixed: E split into E1 (over-claim) / E2 (under-claim), both ship-blockers, principle stated as grade-the-report-against-the-ledger-in-BOTH-directions; C widened to absorb undisclosed recovery; D widened from 'non-retryable' to any fault (its definition had been narrower than its own documented usage); assignment rules added so 7 outcomes map to exactly one class each. idempotent-action-design PASSED 11/11; tester verified the verb table row-by-row and that 'exactly-once' is never asserted across 9 occurrences. META: that tester also refused MY instruction to end every line with 'PASS. Beats baseline.' -- correctly, since normals should often pass at baseline and claiming a win there is the rubber stamp the suite prevents. My template was wrong, not the agent; fixed in EVALS.template + CURATION-LESSONS.

source: last build candidate + the loop's own reflection engine
notes: BIGGEST FINDING OF THE SERIES, and it came from applying a fix rather than from the test. wave-reflect FAILED (14/15): it asserted determinism twice while 3 of 4 rules left the deciding parameter unrecorded (high/low-water 'tune to your domain', window 'N~10', rule 3 with no operational test) and rule 4 rested on a term NO schema field could answer. Fixed with a pinned CONFIG block, an honest restatement (same data + same recorded config -> same lessons), an operational overlap test, and a sources_new field. THEN recomputing under the pinned config made github-practitioner compute to DEPRIORITIZE (n=2, yield 0.00) -- contradicting a CONFIRMED lesson those same waves produced. Cause: yield_rate=adopted/seen scores a PRODUCER by a CONSUMER's outcome; harvest hands candidates to a later build wave, so it read 0.00 for work that produced 10 candidate methods, 7 build-worthy. An automated rule was one pass from deprioritizing the library's best source type on a metric that measured the wrong stage. Fixed in method (candidates field + producer-vs-consumer rule) and instance; standing directive: when a computed verdict contradicts a lesson you trust, suspect the metric before obeying the rule. data-contract-assertions PASSED 13/13; two In-this-repo defects patched, incl. a GUESSED 30pct null figure in the talent whose step 3 says 'Compute, don't guess' -- measured 74pct independently by both the tester and the coordinator.

FIRST wave scored as a PRODUCER (candidates, not adopted) after the measurement fix -- yield 4/61 = 6.6pct, which would have read 0.00 under the old formula. 61 skills examined, 4 candidates queued, 1 deferred (the harvesting agent flagged it as thinnest and offered it as the cut; coordinator agreed since this harvest ran 8pct vs a 1pct baseline), 13 rejected per-candidate. CONVERGENT DISCOVERY: expand-contract sequencing was named independently by BOTH sources, which raised its priority. The two highest-value items are NOT new talents and were recorded as fold-in proposals instead: diagnosing-bugs Phase 1 into systematic-debugging (build a tight already-red repro LOOP before hypothesising; raise the reproduction rate rather than punting on non-reproducible bugs) and expand-contract sequencing into writing-plans. Both harvesting agents refused to make them talents because they collide on TRIGGER -- two talents racing one trigger is a routing bug. 4 security rejections: an auto-running PreToolUse hook writing to .claude/settings.json, a secrets-to-.env wizard, and two CLI installers. Also caught: a source skill whose description would have collided head-on with writing-skills -- adopted second clause only.

notes: First pass run under the post-calibration scenario guidance: adversarial scenarios written as SOCIAL PRESSURE rather than technique traps, and the baseline field forbidden from being written off the scenario label. Both talents FAILED and both defects were the coordinator's own, introduced hours earlier. systematic-debugging: the repro-rate section gated ENTRY to hypothesis on measured evidence but left EXIT ungated -- Phase 4 asks only 'test passes now?', and on a loop reproducing 1 in 50 a single green run appears 98pct of the time with no fix, so a mitigation could ship as a root-cause fix. writing-plans: the rewritten description dropped the second disjunct of its own Scope Check rule, and since the description is the routing surface, a 63-file rename routed to 'edit' while two sections of the body said 'plan'. Also fixed: a self-certifying escape hatch, the missing excuse on the pressure-defence surfaces, and the expand-contract boundary promoted from a trailing parenthetical to a precondition. Two judgment calls raised to the human gate rather than decided. Both auditors deviated from my brief and were right both times -- heading level (avoiding the mis-promoted-heading defect) and refusing to report a green number without saying what the suite cannot see.

job: full KB walk-through (4 read-only judges over 23 candidate pairs + coordinator sweep of all 44 notes): 9 findings applied, 11 proposals surfaced, compiled-page freshness check added
notes: wall_clock_s = 427, MEASURED as the LONGEST of the four judges' own reported durations (229.7s, 301.9s, 309.6s, 426.4s) since they ran concurrently. It covers the fan-out ONLY. An earlier version of this row said 257,618s, computed as now-minus-start: the session was interrupted and resumed across days, so that number measured idle time, not work. It is corrected here rather than left, because a wall_clock that includes waiting is worse than no wall_clock - the whole point of this column is loop cost. The coordinator's own sweep is NOT separable from that idle time and is therefore excluded, which makes 427 a LOWER bound on the pass. agents = 4, the cap; TaskList checked before dispatch, none running. tokens_est MEASURED as the sum of the judges' reported subagent_tokens (100732+95541+80859+117023); excludes the coordinator, so also a lower bound. The deterministic tier was EMPTY before the pass began - 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 contradictions, 0 unargued pairs - so all 9 applied findings came from reading, and 5 were invisible to every existing check for five different structural reasons. Judges read-only by instruction; the coordinator applied every edit, and the lint caught a one-way link the coordinator itself created, before commit. spend_measured null - no metered path.
